Chapter 3: Curious or Tentative.
Picture this—you’ve had a few conversations, maybe exchanged a couple laughs, and now, something shifts. The person across from you starts letting their guard down. There’s a spark of curiosity in their eyes, and you can tell they’re just a little more engaged than before.
Maybe you notice they’re asking more questions. Or they lean in and really listen to what you’re saying. It’s subtle, but it’s real. They’re not fully open yet, but you sense that gentle nudge toward trust.
Why does this phase matter? Well, think about the last time you tried something new—maybe a hobby, or even just trying a new restaurant. At first, you’re cautious, right? But as soon as you get a taste of something interesting, you want to know more. That’s exactly what’s happening here.
The “curious or tentative” stage is all about little signals—body language, the tone of their voice, those small questions that show they’re interested but still testing the waters. It’s kind of like dipping your toes in before diving into the pool.
Here’s something to pay attention to: people in this stage might still be a bit reserved. Maybe they share a little, then pull back to see how you react. It’s perfectly normal. Your job is to create a safe space, answer questions honestly, and show genuine interest in return.
If you handle this moment with patience and warmth, you’ll help them feel more comfortable—and ready to move forward.
So, the next time you notice someone’s curiosity starting to peek through, remember: that’s your opportunity to build trust, one small step at a time.
